title: Feature Sproutpad: Ephemeral Helper Modules (scratch)
content:
Quick brain-dump for a lightweight feature concept: Ephemeral Helper Modules (EHM). Purpose: let product surfaces attach tiny, disposable behavior modules to an LLM response pipeline without shipping full backend services. Think: short-lived plugins that apply small transforms, retrieval lookups, or shallow safety checks for a single request or session.

Why:
- Customers want to test micro-behaviors (e.g., paraphrase tone, strict date filter, inline citations) without a long release cycle.
- Reduces friction for experiments that are orthogonal to core model changes.
- Gives feature teams a low-risk way to compose behavior at the response edge.

Primary goals / success signals:
- <10 lines of config to enable a helper on a route or session
- Can sandbox a module so it never touches customer prompt data outside runtime (privacy constraint)
- Latency impact < 25ms p50 for typical helper actions (heuristic transforms, small vector lookups)
- 5 internal experiments enabled within 8 weeks; at least 1 promoted to production route

Core concepts (rough):
- Module: tiny code/manifest describing an action (transform, enrichment, filter). Stored as versioned manifest + optional artifact (lambda-like).
- Scope: request | session | route. Ephemeral modules default to route:experimental or per-request override via API header.
- Execution sandbox: wasm or restricted JS env with strict time/memory caps. No outbound network by default; allowed connectors declared in manifest.
- Data handling: helpers operate on a copy of the model input/response. By default, no logs persist except for audit identifiers. Must support KMS/HSM for any secret connectors.

Example use-cases / quick sketches:
- Tone clamp: convert all assistant responses to "concise, formal" style (regex + small rule set)
- Inline citation adder: given vector store id and top-k retrieval, inject citation markers where evidence found
- Safety pre-filter: run a fast heuristic classifier to drop or replace risky spans before final tokenization
- Currency normalizer: detect currency mentions and append USD equivalence (small lookup table)
- A/B micro-rollout: attach 2 competing helpers to route and split-by-session to measure quality delta

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /v1/helpers/compile -> returns helper-id (manifest + artifact hash)
- PATCH /v1/routes/:routeId -> attach helper-id with scope & rollout %
- Header override: X-Redwood-Helper: helper-id;X-Redwood-Helper-Scope: request
- Runtime isolation: helpers run with a runtime token; admin-only ops to grant connector access

User stories (MVP scope):
- As a product engineer, I want to upload a tiny helper that rewrites date formats so I can test user-facing formatting without deploying a backend change.
- As an experimenter, I want to enable a helper only for 10% of traffic on a route to measure latency and acceptance.
- As an SRE, I want to see helper-level telemetry (exec time, memory, failures) and easy kill-switches.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Helper manifest spec documented + editor in Console (title, version, declared connectors, allowed ops)
- Runtime can execute a helper that performs a simple string transform end-to-end on a hosted route
- Runtime enforces timeouts (e.g., 50ms default), memory caps, and returns failure semantics that fall back to baseline response
- Console shows per-helper p50/p95 exec time and error rate for last 24h

Metrics to track:
- Activation rate (# routes with helpers / total routes)
- Mean execution time per helper type
- % of fallbacks triggered due to helper failures
- Experiment conversion uplift (qualitative evals or NPS) for promoted helpers

Open questions / risks:
- Security: what connector surface do we allow? If helpers can call customer-owned vector stores, we must prevent sensitive leakage.
- Performance: wasm vs JS vs microservice proxy. wasm looks promising for safety + perf but increases engineering lift.
- Ownership model: who maintains helper catalog? Community contributed vs curated Redwoodsafe modules.
- Billing: charge by execution ms + memory or bundle into route charges? Simpler to start free internal-only.
- Debugging UX: how do teams iterate quickly? REPL in Console? Test harness that runs helper with canned payloads?

Prototype plan (6 week sprint-ish):
- Week 1: narrow manifest spec, minimal helpers (tone clamp, date normalizer). Console wireframe for attach/detach.
- Week 2-3: implement wasm runtime runner (pooled) + manifest store; integrate with dev routes (internal-only).
- Week 4: telemetry + kill-switch; header override support for request-scoped runs.
- Week 5: internal experiment with 3 product teams; gather latency + qualitative feedback.
- Week 6: tidy docs, decide next steps (promote to beta or iterate).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Talk to SRE about sandboxing options (rohit?). Slack thread: #runtime-sandbox (seeded)
- Check legal for data retention rules if helpers access external connectors
- Draft a simple helper manifest example to add to Confluence page (linked above)
- Prototype CLI tool to package small helper archives (tar + manifest)

Quick manifest example (brain sketch):
- id: informal-demo-1
- name: tone-clamp-v0
- version: 0.1.0
- runtime: wasm
- entrypoint: ./main.wasm
- permissions: [read:request, write:response]
- connectors: []

Edge behaviours / fallback semantics (proposal):
- helper success -> merge helper response with model output according to merge policy (replace | patch | annotate)
- helper timeout/error -> log + metric, return baseline model output and mark session for review if error rate > threshold

Next immediate actions:
- Put a 30-min sync on calendar with Maya, Evan, and Rohit to align constraints and SRE feasibility
- Mock Console flow in Figma (basic attach UX)
- Create JIRA epic (JIRA-IF-842) and break into 3 quick tickets: manifest spec, runtime PoC, console attach flow

Why I like this: reduces friction for small experiments, encourages reuse of micro-behaviors, and may serve as a safe onramp for customer-provided lightweight logic in private deployments. But must keep surface limited at first.

Random scribbles / fringe ideas:
- Helper gallery with curated patterns (paraphrase, citation, profanity clamp) that teams can fork
- Version pinning + canary: route pins helper@v1.2; new uploads default to draft until promoted
- Cost-saver: allow combinator optimization where multiple helpers are merged into a single wasm to amortize startup costs

End of scratchpad. Will flesh into PRD if consensus from the sync.
_notes: informal scratch, not a spec. keep in users area
